title: Finite-ring bounded lisse complexes and finite derived isomorphism sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $B$ a finite commutative ring. On the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] use $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and constant coefficient sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. If $K$ is bounded and every cohomology sheaf is locally constant with finite $B$-module stalks, there is an etale covering on which $K$ is isomorphic to the constant sheaf complex associated to a bounded complex of finite $B$-modules. For two such complexes $K,L$, the sheafification on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ of $V\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{D(V_{\mathrm{et}},B)}(K|_V,L|_V)$ is finite locally constant; locally on constant models $E,G$ its fibre is $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(E,G)$. The analogous sheaf of isomorphisms is finite locally constant, possibly empty. On a connected $X$, for any geometric point $\bar x$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], $K$ is etale locally isomorphic to the constant complex $K_{\bar x}$. No finite Tor dimension is assumed.

proof.text: Use the finite locally constant module-values theorem on every cohomology sheaf and every slice. Finite modules over the finite ring are finitely generated. Replace possibly reversed degree bounds a,b by min(a,b),b, which keeps the vanishing hypothesis. Apply the etale-site bounded constant-model theorem to these covering trivializations. It handles transport to a site with matching object and morphism universes and returns the required cover with unchanged support bounds.

Refine the two model covers for K and L by their fiber-product cover. Pullback composition and compatibility with constant sheaves give constant complex models for both restrictions. The presheaf restriction comparison, combined with Mathlib Functor.pushforwardContinuousSheafificationCompatibility for the slice forgetful functor and the etale-site equivalence, identifies restriction of each sheafified mapping presheaf with the corresponding local mapping sheaf. Conjugate by the two model isomorphisms and apply the constant-complex mapping comparison.

Algebraic Hom between the two finite bounded local complexes is finite, and Iso injects into Hom by its forward map. Thus both mapping sheaves are locally constant with finite constant values. For each geometric point choose a lift through the cover; cofinality of the slice neighbourhood category identifies its stalk with the stalk of the restricted constant sheaf, hence with its finite value. This proves finiteness as well as local constancy. The required global constant-Hom comparison is the Hom clause of the constant-complex theorem.

Suppose $X$ is connected and $\bar x$ is a geometric point, and set $E_0=K_{\bar x}$. For each local model $\underline E_j$ on a nonempty cover member $U_j$, exact stalks and the constant-stalk identification give $K_{\bar y}\simeq E_j$ for every geometric point of $U_j$. Define $O\subseteq X$ as the union of the images of those members whose model is isomorphic in $D(B)$ to $E_0$. These images are open because etale morphisms are open. The complement is the union of the images of the other members: an overlap would give a geometric point and identify their two fibres, contradicting the different isomorphism classes. Thus $O$ is both open and closed and contains $x$. Connectedness forces $O=X$. Every nonempty member therefore has $E_j\simeq E_0$, and composing this algebraic isomorphism with its local-model isomorphism gives an etale covering trivializing $K$ as $\underline{K_{\bar x}}$. This proves the connected clause globally, not only near $\bar x$. No step used a finite Tor bound. The empty scheme has no geometric point, so this clause is vacuous. Stalk identifications used here respect the $B$-action, since they are natural for multiplication by each $b\in B$.

The statement is identical to the base copy. The delivery has no new nodes and no cycle. Step 1 meets the site-bounded-constant-model hypotheses: a finite ring is Noetherian, finite stalks come from the constant-stalk lemma, and empty members can take the zero model. Step 2 satisfies the stronger finite-cone hypothesis because every cone term is a finite set. Steps 3 and 4 are correct: the stupid truncation gives H^i(C)=0 for i>=m, orthogonality and both parts of the Hom-out-of-triangle node give the precomposition bijection, and constant-exact works on finite cycles, boundaries and cohomology. Steps 5 and 6 are correct: 08FR (1) and (2), the locally-constant-hom lemma and natural stalks give local surjectivity and injectivity, and the 00WB/00WK sections node gives the bijection of sheafifications. Step 7 is correct: def-kun gives a constant functor on D(B), and stalks detect isomorphisms. Step 8 is correct: etale maps are open, overlaps give a common geometric point, and connectedness does the rest. I checked B=Z/4 with E=G=Z/2 by hand: the chain-map count gives Hom=Z/2 with no Tor assumption. I also checked zero complexes, an empty Isom, an empty X and disconnected X. I searched for duplicates: the sfb nodes need a perfect source and are not duplicates. I accept the declared tool use of lem-pc-ring-finite-cone-free-model (Stacks 064U), which is generic algebra. The other nodes are in the unit's route or are Mathlib leaves. No changes.
